results.reason: Issue 3 flags SA § 13.2. It notes that Supplier may assign to any third party without consent or notice while Customer is restricted. It explains the risk to supply continuity and to Customer drawings reaching a competitor, and recommends mutual consent, a competitor carve-out and notice.

Issue 1 flags SA § 13.3: Customer change of control requires Supplier's prior written consent, and Supplier may terminate if the sale closes without it. It ties this to the pending sale and recommends deleting the clause, limiting it to competitors with consent not unreasonably withheld, or obtaining a waiver before signing or closing.
The memo never identifies the automatic renewal in OF § 2.2, the 30-day non-renewal notice window, or the three-year renewal terms. It mentions only the Initial Term.

Issue 2 flags SA § 9.3, which excludes Customer's § 10.1 indemnity from the cap. It explains that Customer's exposure is unlimited while Supplier's indemnity stays capped, and recommends deleting § 9.3 or making any carve-out mutual and narrow.
The memo correctly states the 12-month fees cap (§ 9.1), Delaware governing law (§ 12.1), and a three-year Initial Term from March 1, 2026.
The memo states the order of precedence (SA, then OF, then Spec) under SA 1.3. It applies it to explain that nothing in the Order Form or Spec softens § 13.3, and notes the Spec sits last.
The memo states an explicit raise order: change of control first, uncapped indemnity second, then assignment. The issues are tiered HIGH and HIGH/MEDIUM.
Each issue has a Where / Why it matters / Recommended fix structure with proposed language. A closing section covers open questions and business decisions for Calder Ridge.
The memo says the Specifications Schedule has no problematic term. It cites no statutes, cases or outside authority, and invents no significant issues.
